claims.value: In 1935, the government promoted Iran in place of Persia as the foreign-language designation of the existing country. Iran was already an established internal name; this naming change did not found a new state or replace the Pahlavi dynasty.

geographicScope.description: Country designation in foreign usage under the assigned existing Reza Shah/Pahlavi political framework; not a territorial boundary or succession claim.

evidence.note: Scholarly Pahlavi nationalism section explicitly dates the Western-language designation change to 1935; year is retained, with no exact commencement day claimed.

Background naming paragraph dates the governmental change to 1935 and identifies Iran as a centuries-old internal designation. Earlier dynastic history distinguishes naming from state/dynasty creation.

cautions: Year precision is deliberate. This event must not become a new polity mapping, a 1935 founding date, or an inferred border/succession change.

sources.title: Iranian Identity iv. In the 19th and 20th Centuries
sources.usage: Read scholarly article body, especially The Rise of State Nationalism in the Pahlavi Era, paragraphs around the four historical innovations: Western-language country designation changed from Persia to Iran in 1935. Source supplies year precision only. Nationalist racial/primordial explanations are analyzed as historical ideology, not adopted as biological fact.

sources.institution: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum, Holocaust Encyclopedia
